reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the feasibility of ball milling and SPS for producing corrosion-resistant Mg alloys and mentions passive film formation, but it does not provide any data or observations on aging-induced grain-boundary precipitation, its effect on corrosion pathways, or its role in high-temperature oxidation. The key mechanistic premises about aging and its dual functional benefits are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Ball milling and SPS can produce nanocrystalline Mg-containing alloys with high hardness and corrosion resistance
Corrosion resistance in such alloys is linked to the formation of a Ti-rich surface film
Aging at 300°C can induce grain-boundary intermetallic precipitates in a nanocrystalline HEA
Grain-boundary precipitates can block intergranular corrosion pathways
Grain-boundary precipitates can promote a dense, protective oxide scale during high-temperature oxidation
